title: Is F45 Worth It in NZ? — Honest Review for 2026
meta_desc: Find out if F45 is worth the cost in NZ. Compare prices, contracts and results with other HIIT options in our 2026 honest review.
intro: F45 has become a buzzword in New Zealand fitness circles, but does the hype match the price? We break down the numbers, contracts and real results so you can decide if it fits your budget and goals.

cta.text: Compare F45 vs other HIIT gyms

sections.heading: What You Get in a 45‑Minute Session
list: 45 minutes of high‑intensity interval training split into 3 functional blocks
Team‑based environment with a trainer leading each block
Access to the F45 app for tracking workouts and nutrition tips
Rotating workout library – no repeats for 12 weeks

sections.heading: Who Benefits Most from F45
list: People who thrive on group motivation and competition
Those looking for a structured, time‑efficient workout (45 min)
Fitness enthusiasts who enjoy constantly varied routines
Clients comfortable with a moderate to high injury‑risk intensity

sections.heading: Contract Terms & Commitment
sections.body: F45 primarily offers two membership routes:
list: 12‑month contract – $199‑$205 per month, 12‑month minimum, $150 early termination fee
Month‑to‑month – $259‑$265 per month, no lock‑in but higher price

sections.heading: Final Verdict & Recommendation
sections.body: If you love the buzz of a team‑driven class and can commit to a 12‑month contract, F45 offers solid value for the price, especially compared with drop‑in rates at other HIIT studios. However, if you prefer lower ongoing costs or more flexibility, Les Mills GRIT or 1RXP provide comparable results at a slightly cheaper month‑to‑month rate.
